text:
Nobody in the league has more goals than Kirill Kaprizov's 17, and he has added 18 assists for 35 points in 21 games. He is on a 10-game point streak (6 goals, 12 assists), and when Matt Boldy scored a hat trick in Toronto on Thursday, Kaprizov set up three goals himself.

He is shooting 25%, against 17% last season, and has 17 goals on 13.3 expected (expected goals measure the quality of the chances he gets). Minnesota has also scored 6.6 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice. The chances are real and plentiful; that finishing rate is what rarely lasts a whole season.

Even with some cooling built in, our range has him finishing between about 95 and 124 points, with 109 in the middle. His goals have also swung results: fourth of 522 skaters in our wins added, helped by an overtime power-play winner against Montreal.

What to watch: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 57% of his entries last season, and carry-ins led to a chance 25% of the time against 8% for dump-ins.
